full_text_en:
Qian Bifang and Huaning Company v. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company,
Zhu Ming'an and Wang Xianchen — Dispute over Shareholder Rights

【Ruling Summary】

In the course of mediation proceedings, where a shareholders' meeting of a limited liability company is convened under the auspices of a people's court and produces a "Shareholders' Meeting Resolution" concerning issues such as equity transfer, the company's claims and debts, and the disposition of assets, that resolution is binding on all shareholders. Therefore, if a shareholder of that limited liability company subsequently initiates a new lawsuit on matters addressed in the Shareholders' Meeting Resolution, the court shall, unless the case falls under circumstances where support is legally warranted, order the parties to respectively comply with and execute the shareholders' meeting resolution.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2005) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 25

Appellants (Defendants at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiffs): Qian Bifang, female, born October 4, 1964, Han nationality, native of Minqing County, Fujian Province, residing at Room 203, Building 51, No. 1 Haifu Lane, Baixia District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Agent ad litem: Zhao Jun, attorney at Beijing Mingtai Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Chen Wenhong, attorney at Beijing Mingtai Law Firm.

Appellants (Defendants at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiffs): Jiangsu Huaning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 10-1 Shihui Lane, Qinhuai District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Qian Jiuzhong, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Zhao Jun, attorney at Beijing Mingtai Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Chen Wenhong, attorney at Beijing Mingtai Law Firm.

Appellees (Plaintiffs at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendants): Zhu Changchun, male, born July 2, 1951, Han nationality, native of Ezhou City, Hubei Province, residing at Zhujiawan, Lianhua Village, Echeng District, Ezhou City, Hubei Province.
Agent ad litem: Cao Li, attorney at Jiangsu Nanjing Hailang Law Firm.

Appellees (Plaintiffs at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendants): Jiangsu Huayu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at South Jinsheng Road, Dongshan Town, Jiangning District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Zhu Changchun, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Cao Li, attorney at Jiangsu Nanjing Hailang Law Firm.

Appellee (Third Party at First Instance): Zhu Ming'an (father of Zhu Changchun), male, born December 5, 1927, Han nationality, native of Ezhou City, Hubei Province, residing at Zhujiawan, Lianhua Village, Echeng District, Ezhou City, Hubei Province.
Agent ad litem: Cao Li, attorney at Jiangsu Nanjing Hailang Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Wang Xianchen (mother of Qian Bifang), female, born July 27, 1943, Han nationality, native of Minqing County, Fujian Province, temporarily residing at Room 203, Building 51, No. 1 Haifu Lane, Baixia District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

In the case of dispute over shareholder rights between appellants Qian Bifang and Jiangsu Huaning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huaning Company) and appellees Zhu Changchun, Jiangsu Huayu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huayu Company), Zhu Ming'an, and third party Wang Xianchen, the Jiangsu High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2004) Su Min Er Chu Zi No. 6 on November 15, 2004. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a hearing on April 26, 2005. Qian Bifang and Zhao Jun, the agent ad litem for both Qian Bifang and Huaning Company, and Cao Li, the agent ad litem for Zhu Changchun, Huayu Company, and Zhu Ming'an, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The facts found by the court of first instance are as follows: Huaning Company was incorporated on March 9, 1999, by Zhu Changchun, Li Qianlin, and Wang Xinmin, with a registered capital of RMB 10 million, of which Zhu Changchun contributed RMB 3.4 million, and Li Qianlin and Wang Xinmin each contributed RMB 3.3 million. On November 12, 1999, Wang Xinmin transferred his equity interests of RMB 1.5 million to Qian Bifang, RMB 1.2 million to Gu Dazhong, and RMB 600,000 to Zhu Changchun. On March 27, 2001, Li Qianlin transferred his entire equity interests of RMB 3.3 million in the company, consisting of RMB 3 million to Zhu Changchun and RMB 300,000 to Qian Bifang, and Gu Dazhong transferred his entire equity interests of RMB 1.2 million in the company to Qian Bifang. After the transfers, the registered capital of the company remained unchanged, with Zhu Changchun contributing RMB 7 million, representing 70% of the registered capital, and Qian Bifang contributing RMB 3 million, representing 30% of the registered capital. On April 10, 2002, the registered capital of Huaning Company was increased to RMB 20 million, with Zhu Changchun contributing RMB 14 million and Qian Bifang contributing RMB 6 million, and their respective proportions of the registered capital remained unchanged. Zhu Changchun served as the chairman of the board, and Qian Bifang served as the general manager of the company.

Huayu Company was incorporated on January 3, 2001, upon application by Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang, with a registered capital of RMB 10 million, of which Zhu Changchun contributed RMB 7.5 million, representing 75% of the registered capital, and Qian Bifang contributed RMB 2.5 million, representing 25% of the registered capital. Zhu Changchun served as the chairman of the board and general manager.

Due to conflicts between Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang in the joint operation of the companies, the parties entered into the "Shareholders' Meeting Resolution of Jiangsu Huaning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Huaning Resolution") on November 12, 2002, which stipulated: Zhu Changchun shall transfer his equity in Huaning Company to Wang Xianchen in a lump sum at a price equivalent to a certain number of RMB yuan; the equity transfer agreement shall be separately signed; the parties agreed that various taxes, fees, outstanding debts, repair costs, and quality compensation factors had been considered in the aforementioned transfer price; after the transfer of equity, Zhu Changchun shall no longer hold any position in Huaning Company and shall deliver all company certificates, seals, contracts, loan and debt evidence, accounting vouchers, etc., in his custody to Qian Bifang on the day the audit report is issued; after Zhu Changchun's equity transfer, the relevant claims and debts left by Huaning Company, disputes with homeowners, and coordination work with relevant departments shall be handled by Qian Bifang and the new shareholder, with Zhu Changchun providing active cooperation; the parties agreed that immediately after this resolution, an audit of Huaning Company's financial assets shall be conducted by an auditing institution of Qinhuai District; immediately after the completion of the audit, procedures for the equity transfer and amendment of the company's business registration shall be carried out; the parties agreed that the Bishuiwan project of Huaning Company and the Bishuiwan West Garden project of Huayu Company shall be exchanged for management after soliciting opinions from the two property management companies and the homeowners; the parties agreed that the Jiajiadian premises shall be handed over to Qian Bifang for management and use, the Hunan Road premises shall be temporarily handed over to Qian Bifang for office use, and the Bishuiwan on-site sales office shall belong to Huaning Company; the parties agreed that the salaries and bonuses for all staff of Huaning Company and Huayu Company for the year 2002 shall be paid by Huayu Company in a lump sum; before the company's audit report is issued, all external expenditures of the company shall be immediately suspended, and Zhu Changchun shall not sign external contracts or sell houses, nor transfer bank funds or real estate; the parties agreed that the cut-off date for the audit shall be November 12, 2002, and the parties shall instruct company employees to actively cooperate; if delays occur due to employees' failure to cooperate truthfully and promptly, Zhu Changchun shall be liable to compensate Qian Bifang; Zhu Changchun agreed that Qian Bifang may register and establish a new company in the near future; other matters not covered shall be resolved through separate negotiation between the parties.

Because the Huaning Resolution was not actually performed, Qian Bifang filed a lawsuit with the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as the Jiangning District Court) on December 12, 2002, seeking division of the properties of Huaning Company and Huayu Company. After the Jiangning District Court accepted the case as (2003) Jiangning Min Yi Zi No. 17, upon Qian Bifang's application, it froze RMB 13.75 million in bank deposits of Huaning Company. Through mediation by the Jiangning District Court, Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang signed the "Shareholders' Meeting Resolution of Jiangsu Huaning Huayu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Huaning Huayu Resolution") on January 23, 2003. Article 1 of the Huaning Huayu Resolution stipulated: Through negotiation between the parties, Zhu Changchun shall transfer all of his equity in Huaning Company (RMB 14 million) to Wang Xianchen in a lump sum, and Qian Bifang shall transfer all of her equity in Huayu Company (RMB 2.5 million) to Zhu Ming'an in a lump sum; the equity transfer agreements shall be separately signed. Article 2 of the Huaning Huayu Resolution stipulated: After the parties sign the equity transfer agreements, each party shall no longer hold any position in the other's company and shall deliver all relevant company certificates, seals, files, documents, contracts, loan and debt evidence, etc., in their respective custody to the other party on the same day. Adjustments to the assets, claims, and debts of the two companies are as follows: 1. Huaning Company shall pay RMB 6 million to Huayu Company; 2. If Huaning Company recovers the 460-mu plot of land on Chengbei Road, it shall pay RMB 14 million to Huayu Company; if cash is recovered, it shall pay 70% of the amount to Huayu Company; 3. The issue of the 28-mu land use right of Huaning Company's Bishuiwan project shall be handled by Zhu Changchun; if it cannot be resolved and additional land premium payments, fines, etc., arise, these shall be borne by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company; 4. When Huaning Company and Huayu Company settle their corporate income tax for the year 2003, 70% of the income tax payable as listed in the actual report shall be borne by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company, and 30% by Qian Bifang and Huaning Company; 5. The unsold villas in Huaning Company's Bishuiwan project, specifically Villas 45, 18, 19, 20, 48, 95, 9, 10, 12, 15, and 17, shall belong to Huaning Company; the remaining villas, specifically Villas 96, 21, 49, 69, 70, 72, 16-2, 32-1, and 66-2, shall belong to Huayu Company; three shops, three villas, and six apartments in Bishuiwan West Garden shall belong to Huaning Company; the remainder shall belong to Huayu Company; all clubhouses shall belong to Huayu Company; 6. The claim of Huaning Company against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau of Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as the Jiangning District Construction Bureau), in the amount of RMB 16.5 million (tentative), shall be recovered by Zhu Changchun; after paying within 30 days the maintenance fund for the Bishuiwan community (approximately RMB 3.5 million), the maintenance fund for Ziwei Garden (approximately RMB 1.96 million), the preliminary demolition costs for the Bishuiwan community of RMB 1.2 million, and the road repair costs for the Bishuiwan community of approximately RMB 1 million, the balance shall belong to Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company; 7. The mutual claims and debts between Huaning Company and Huayu Company as of January 22, 2003, shall be set off against each other, and no further recovery shall be made; 8. Except for the items listed above, the other assets and liabilities of Huaning Company and Huayu Company shall be separately enjoyed and handled by each company. Article 3 of the Huaning Huayu Resolution stipulated: After the parties sign the "Equity Transfer Agreements," legal procedures for amending the business registration and adjusting the company's assets shall be carried out under the supervision of the Jiangning District Court.

On the same day the Huaning Huayu Resolution was signed, the parties also signed a "Supplementary Resolution" stipulating: Huaning Company shall bear the unpaid construction costs for the Bishuiwan and Ziwei Garden projects up to RMB 5.5 million; the portion exceeding RMB 5.5 million shall be paid by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company; the construction costs shall be confirmed by Zhu Changchun and then paid by Qian Bifang.

On January 23, 2003, the Jiangning District Court organized the parties for the handover. Qian Bifang issued to Zhu Changchun a transfer check of Huaning Company for RMB 5.2 million to fulfill the obligation to pay RMB 6 million to Huayu Company; the parties agreed that this amount would be paid from the funds frozen by the Jiangning District Court, and to facilitate payment, the Jiangning District Court would lift the freeze on the aforementioned account. Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang signed the relevant legal documents for transferring the equity of Huaning Company and Huayu Company and handed them to Qian Bifang's attorney for unified processing. Qian Bifang, on behalf of Huaning Company, signed the relevant legal documents transferring the claim of Huaning Company against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau to Huayu Company and handed them to Zhu Changchun. Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang signed an agreement regarding the distribution of the land price refund from the Jiangning District Land and Resources Administration Bureau of Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as the Jiangning District Land Bureau).

On January 24, 2003, the Jiangning District Court lifted the freeze on RMB 13.65 million in bank deposits of Huaning Company. However, when Zhu Changchun presented the check for RMB 5.2 million to the bank where Huaning Company maintained its account, he was informed that the check was a bad check. The RMB 13.65 million in deposits of Huaning Company that had been frozen by the Jiangning District Court and subsequently unfrozen had been entirely withdrawn by Qian Bifang. The Jiangning District Court served by mail a notice dated January 24, 2003, granting Qian Bifang's withdrawal of the lawsuit.

On December 1, 2004, Qian Bifang and Wang Xianchen amended the business registration of Huaning Company, changing the shareholder from Zhu Changchun to Wang Xianchen and changing the legal representative to Qian Jiuzhong (father of Qian Bifang).

Qian Bifang and Huaning Company also went to the Jiangning District Construction Bureau to directly assert the claim that had been transferred to Huayu Company.

Huaning Company paid the following taxes: corporate income tax of RMB 35,514.55 for the tax period January to December 2002, paid on April 29, 2003; corporate income tax of RMB 186,304.15 for the tax period April to June 2003, paid on July 15, 2003; corporate income tax of RMB 20,485.55 for the tax period January to September 2003, paid on October 16, 2003; general business tax of RMB 237,118.70, education surtax of RMB 9,484.75, and urban maintenance and construction tax of RMB 16,598.31 for the tax period February 2003, paid on March 6, 2003; and other stamp taxes totaling RMB 5,164.75, and general business tax, education surtax, and urban maintenance and construction tax totaling RMB 5,790.22 for the tax period 2003, paid on January 17, 2004.

After January 23, 2003, Huaning Company claimed that it had paid a total of RMB 3,228,078 in various construction costs for the Bishuiwan and Ziwei Garden projects.

Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company filed an action with the court of first instance, alleging: Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang were shareholders and jointly owned Huaning Company and Huayu Company. Huaning Company and Huayu Company were companies with common shareholders, and there were many connections between the two companies in terms of fund flows, personnel, etc. Qian Bifang, as a shareholder of Huaning Company and Huayu Company, believed that the majority shareholder Zhu Changchun had harmed the company's interests and her shareholder rights in the course of operations, and indicated that she could no longer continue to cooperate with Zhu Changchun. She previously filed a lawsuit with the Jiangning District Court on December 12, 2002, seeking division of the properties of Huaning Company and Huayu Company. After the Jiangning District Court accepted the case, upon Qian Bifang's application, it froze RMB 13.75 million in bank deposits of Huaning Company.

During mediation by the Jiangning District Court, Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang signed the Huaning Huayu Resolution on January 23, 2003, stipulating: 1. Zhu Changchun agreed to transfer his 70% equity in Huaning Company to Wang Xianchen free of charge, and Qian Bifang agreed to transfer her 25% equity in Huayu Company to Zhu Ming'an free of charge. 2. The assets between Huayu Company and Huaning Company were adjusted as follows: (1) Huaning Company shall pay RMB 6 million to Huayu Company; (2) the villas in Bishuiwan, Jiangning District, Nanjing (Villas 96, 21, 49, 69, 70, 16-2, 32-1, 66-2) owned by Huaning Company shall be transferred free of charge to Huayu Company and registered under its name; (3) the claim of RMB 16.5 million held by Huaning Company against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau shall be transferred to Huayu Company in the form of an assignment of claims; (4) 70% of the claim held by Huaning Company against the Jiangning District Land Bureau, i.e., RMB 14 million, shall belong to Huayu Company. The third parties involved in this resolution expressed no objection and were willing to cooperate in performance. On January 23, 2003, the parties conducted the following handovers under the organization of the Jiangning District Court: (1) Qian Bifang issued to Zhu Changchun a transfer check of Huaning Company for RMB 5.2 million to fulfill the obligation to pay Huayu Company; the funds were to be paid from the frozen account of the Jiangning District Court; to facilitate payment, the Jiangning District Court would lift the freeze on the said account; (2) Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang signed the relevant legal documents for transferring the equity of Huaning Company and Huayu Company and handed them to Qian Bifang's attorney for unified processing; (3) Qian Bifang, on behalf of Huaning Company, signed the relevant legal documents transferring the claim of Huaning Company against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau to Huayu Company and handed them to Zhu Changchun; (4) Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang signed an agreement regarding the distribution of the land price refund from the Jiangning District Land Bureau.

On January 24, 2003, the Jiangning District Court lifted the freeze on the RMB 13.65 million in deposits of Huaning Company. When Zhu Changchun went to the bank where Huaning Company maintained its account to cash the check for RMB 5.2 million, he was informed that the check was a bad check.

Since January 24, 2003, Huaning Company has been actually controlled and operated by Qian Bifang, and Huayu Company has been actually controlled and operated by Zhu Changchun. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company have not paid the above-mentioned RMB 5.2 million to date.

On December 1, 2003, Qian Bifang and Wang Xianchen amended the business registration of Huaning Company, changing the shareholder from Zhu Changchun to Wang Xianchen and changing the legal representative to Qian Jiuzhong (father of Qian Bifang).

Because Qian Bifang has not cooperated in transferring her equity in Huayu Company to Zhu Ming'an, the shareholders registered in the business registration of Huayu Company remain Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company also have not transferred the relevant real estate to Huayu Company as agreed. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company went to the Jiangning District Construction Bureau to directly assert the claim that had been transferred to Huayu Company, causing Huayu Company to be unable to realize the claim interest. Furthermore, as to the claim of Huaning Company against the Jiangning District Land Bureau, Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company have also been unable to enjoy it. In summary, Qian Bifang and Huaning Company have not performed any of the obligations under the Huaning Huayu Resolution. Accordingly, the plaintiffs requested: 1. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company shall jointly and severally pay RMB 5.2 million to Huayu Company; 2. Huaning Company shall transfer the title of the villas located in Bishuiwan, Jiangning District, Nanjing (Villas 96, 21, 49, 69, 70, 72, 16-2, 32-1, 66-2) to Huayu Company; if such transfer is not possible, Qian Bifang and Huaning Company shall jointly and severally pay a consideration of approximately RMB 15 million (actual value to be determined by market appraisal); 3. Huaning Company shall transfer its claim of RMB 16.5 million against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau to Huayu Company; 4. Huaning Company shall transfer 70% of its claim against the Jiangning District Land Bureau (i.e., RMB 14 million) to Huayu Company; 5. Qian Bifang shall assist Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company in transferring her 25% equity (capital contribution of RMB 2.5 million) in Huayu Company to Zhu Ming'an; 6. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company shall bear the litigation costs of this case.

Qian Bifang responded in her defense: The legal representatives of both Huaning Company and Huayu Company were Zhu Changchun, and the actual management rights of the two companies were also long held by Zhu Changchun, while Qian Bifang was responsible for sales. Because Zhu Changchun concealed business information, privately registered and established a competing company, and engaged in improper conduct such as concealing company assets and making mistakes in land investment, Qian Bifang demanded a liquidation of company assets to protect her own legitimate rights and interests. On November 12, 2002, the two parties signed the "Huaning Resolution" stipulating: (1) Zhu Changchun would transfer his equity in Huaning Company to Wang Xianchen in a one-time transfer and withdraw from the operation of Huaning Company; (2) The two parties would jointly entrust an audit institution to audit the financial status of Huaning Company as of November 12, 2002, and all external expenditures of the company would be suspended immediately until the audit report was issued. However, thereafter, during the trial of the case by the Jiangning District Court, Jiangsu Zhongxing Certified Public Accountants conducted a preliminary audit of the two companies. On January 23, 2003, the two parties reached the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" and the "Supplemental Resolution." On January 23, 2003, under the auspices of the Jiangning District Court, the two parties further reached an agreement on relevant matters: (1) Huaning Company would pay Huayu Company RMB 5.2 million; (2) The real estate properties of Huaning Company and Huayu Company would no longer be adjusted. On the same day, Qian Bifang and Zhu Changchun signed the "Debt Transfer and Collection Authorization Agreement" in the Jiangning District Court, and the two parties exchanged the seals of the two companies. Qian Bifang issued an undated check for RMB 5.2 million to Huayu Company (Qian Bifang requested that Zhu Changchun fulfill the agreement and clear the documents on the same day before the check would be honored). However: 1. Zhu Changchun failed to deliver the Huaning Company documents to Huaning Company on the same day as agreed, making it impossible for Qian Bifang to verify the amount of outstanding project funds owed by Huaning Company. The book balance of Huaning Company's outstanding project funds was over RMB 10 million. Qian Bifang repeatedly demanded from Zhu Changchun the portion of project funds exceeding RMB 5.5 million that he was contractually obligated to bear, but to no avail. After the seal handover, Qian Bifang checked with the bank and discovered that the book balance of Huaning Company differed from the actual bank balance by over RMB 5 million. Because Zhu Changchun refused to explain the whereabouts, blocking the honor of Zhu Changchun's RMB 5.2 million check was Qian Bifang's self-rescue measure. 2. According to the agreement between the two parties, Zhu Changchun was to hold a power of attorney to exercise claims against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau and transfer the funds into Huaning Company's account for payment of the four expenses mentioned above. However, to date, Huaning Company has not received a single cent. Huaning Company had no choice but to revoke its authorization to Zhu Changchun, assert the claim against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau on its own, and is preparing to resolve the matter through litigation. 3. Huaning Company repeatedly demanded from the Jiangning District Land Bureau the 460 mu of land at Chengbei Road or the return of the RMB 20 million deposit and advance payment for the land transfer fee, but was refused each time. It is now preparing to resolve the matter through arbitration. 4. After Qian Bifang took over Huaning Company, it was never able to conduct normal business operations for the following reasons: During the period when Zhu Changchun was in charge of operations, disputes over the quality of the Bishuiwan Project and delays in delivering houses led to customer claims, resulting in nearly twenty lawsuits. Huaning Company compensated customers with nearly RMB 1 million. Because there were no project documents, outstanding project funds could not be calculated or paid, resulting in numerous construction teams repeatedly blocking the offices of Huaning Company, almost paralyzing the company. 5. The corporate income tax for 2003, after final settlement, still required a tax payment of RMB 25 million. According to the agreement, Zhu Changchun should bear 70%, i.e., RMB 17.5 million, but Zhu Changchun has refused to bear this amount to date.

Therefore, Qian Bifang argued: 1. Because Zhu Changchun's refusal to deliver the Huaning Company project documents prevented Huaning Company from verifying the outstanding project funds and the amount that Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company should share, blocking the honor of his check was an act of self-help and also a lawful act of exercising the right of concurrent performance defense. Therefore, since Zhu Changchun had not concurrently performed his obligation, his claim for payment of RMB 5.2 million should be dismissed. 2. Because the parties in dispute had already clarified during the mediation on January 23, 2003, that the real estate properties of Huaning Company and Huayu Company would no longer be adjusted, Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company's claim for Qian Bifang and Huaning Company to change the ownership of eight villas or pay compensation of RMB 15 million had no contractual or legal basis and should be dismissed according to law. 3. Because the parties in dispute had agreed that the balance of the claim against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau, after being realized and used to pay the four expenses of Huaning Company, would belong to Huayu Company, and the conditions for the transfer of the claim had not yet been fulfilled, Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company's claim for the transfer of this RMB 16.5 million claim to Huayu Company violated the agreement between the parties and should be dismissed according to law. 4. Because Huaning Company's claim against the Jiangning District Land Bureau could not be transferred by the nature of the contract (it did not meet the statutory conditions for the transfer of land use rights), and Huaning Company had not yet obtained the rights or received corresponding compensation, Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company's claim for the acquisition of the RMB 14 million claim against the Jiangning District Land Bureau had no factual or legal basis and should be dismissed according to law. 5. Because Zhu Changchun refused to bear the unpaid taxes, and Huaning Company's assets were mainly reflected as accounts receivable from Huayu Company, Qian Bifang and Huaning Company were objectively unable to bear the taxes due on their own. Before this issue was properly resolved, they refused to transfer their equity in Huayu Company.

Qian Bifang and Huaning Company filed a counterclaim, stating: The two parties signed the "Huaning Resolution" on November 12, 2002, the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" on January 23, 2003, and the "Supplemental Resolution" on the same day. After the signing of the above agreements, Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company failed to perform according to the agreements, infringing upon the legitimate rights and interests of Qian Bifang and Huaning Company. The main facts and reasons are as follows: (1) Regarding the tax payable by Huaning Company. According to the provisions of the "Huaning Huayu Resolution," when calculating the corporate income tax for 2003 for Huaning Company and Huayu Company, 70% of the income tax payable as listed in the audit report of the accounting firm would be borne by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company. During the period when Zhu Changchun controlled Huaning Company, he left behind a large number of tax issues but failed to inform Qian Bifang and Huaning Company of the tax payable status, and also refused to deliver the relevant project and financial documents, making it impossible for Huaning Company to accurately calculate the tax payable. Huaning Company could only pre-pay the 2003 tax of Huaning Company in the amount of RMB 242,304.49 based on existing documents and also paid RMB 120,000 on behalf of Huayu Company for tax investigation and supplementary payments. The opposing party should bear 70% of the above pre-paid income tax of RMB 242,304.49 for 2003. The tax payable by Huaning Company after the relevant documents are handed over and calculated or after tax authorities verify and supplement should also be borne by the opposing party at 70%. (2) Regarding the portion of project funds exceeding RMB 5.5 million. The "Supplemental Resolution" stipulated: "As of January 22, 2003, the unpaid project funds (various items) for the Ziwei Garden and Bishuiwan projects of Huaning Company, in the portion of RMB 5.5 million or less, shall be paid by Huaning Company and Qian Bifang; the portion exceeding RMB 5.5 million shall be the responsibility of Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company. Payment of project funds shall be made by Qian Bifang after confirmation by Zhu Changchun." After the resolution was made, because the opposing party refused to deliver the project documents and related contracts and files, it has been impossible to determine the amount of outstanding project funds to date. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company now request the court to entrust an audit institution to audit the outstanding project funds to determine the amount that Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company should bear. (3) Regarding company documents and project documents. According to the agreement, after both parties signed the "Equity Transfer Agreement," neither party would hold any position in the other party's company, and would hand over to the other party on the same day all certificates, seals, archives, documents, contracts, and debt and credit certificates in their respective possession. To date, Zhu Changchun has not fulfilled this contractual obligation. (4) Regarding the vehicles. Four vehicles owned by Huaning Company—a Buick (Su A-T6921), an Iveco (Su A-49440), a Santana (Su A-51772), and a Changhe (Su A-T5045)—are still in the possession and use of the opposing party, who has repeatedly refused to return them despite multiple demands. (5) Regarding losses caused to Huaning Company by Zhu Changchun. During the period when Zhu Changchun operated Huaning Company, due to strategic missteps in management, expenses including garden area refunds, project maintenance costs, and compensation amounts totaled RMB 1,060,082. This amount should be borne by Zhu Changchun. (6) Zhu Changchun improperly used RMB 7,385,582.57 of Huaning Company's funds. Article 11 of the "Huaning Resolution" stipulated: Before the company's audit report is issued, all external expenditures of the company shall be suspended immediately, and Zhu Changchun shall not sign contracts or sell houses externally, nor shall he transfer bank funds or real estate. However, from November 12, 2002, to January 23, 2003, Zhu Changchun improperly used RMB 7,385,582.57 of Huaning Company's funds to pay outstanding project funds for the Bishuiwan West Garden, whereas the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" signed on January 23, 2003, stipulated that the unsold portion of the Bishuiwan West Garden community would belong to Huayu Company, and Zhu Changchun would no longer be a shareholder of Huaning Company. This shows that Zhu Changchun had obvious tortious conduct, and Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company should return the above amount. (7) Zhu Ming'an should pay corresponding consideration for the transfer of equity in Huayu Company. According to the agreement between the two parties, Qian Bifang transferred her 25% equity in Huayu Company to Zhu Ming'an. After the agreement was signed, Qian Bifang no longer participated in the affairs of Huayu Company. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company argue that Zhu Ming'an, in requesting to receive this 25% equity in Huayu Company, should pay corresponding consideration. Now that Zhu Changchun and others have refused to pay the corresponding consideration, the value of Huayu Company's assets as of January 23, 2003, should be audited to determine the amount of consideration that Zhu Changchun and Zhu Ming'an should pay. (8) Regarding the handling of debts and claims concealed by Zhu Changchun during the period he controlled Huaning Company. Before January 23, 2003, Huaning Company was actually controlled and operated by Zhu Changchun. During the negotiations between the parties, Zhu Changchun concealed a large number of debts and claims. In addition to those listed above, the debts of Huaning Company concealed by Zhu Changchun should be borne by him personally, and the concealed claims and income should be returned to Qian Bifang and Huaning Company. In summary, the actions of Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company have infringed upon the rights and interests of Qian Bifang and Huaning Company and have seriously affected the normal operations of Huaning Company. Accordingly, they request: 1. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company bear 70% of the pre-paid 2003 corporate income tax of Huaning Company in the amount of RMB 242,304.49, i.e., RMB 169,613.14; bear 70% of the corporate income tax payable by Huaning Company that has not yet been determined due to incomplete documents, approximately RMB 12,000; 2. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company bear 70% of the general business tax, stamp tax, etc., already paid by Huaning Company totaling RMB 274,156.73, i.e., RMB 191,909.71; bear 70% of other taxes payable by Huaning Company not yet confirmed by tax authorities (business tax and surcharges, land value-added tax, stamp tax, etc.), approximately RMB 14,000; 3. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company bear the portion of various project funds payable by Huaning Company as of January 23, 2003, as confirmed by audit, that exceeds RMB 5.5 million, approximately RMB 1.5 million; 4. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company return all company documents and project documents belonging to Huaning Company; 5. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company return the four vehicles owned by Huaning Company: Buick (Su A-T6921) valued at RMB 357,368, Iveco (Su A-49440) valued at RMB 147,643, Santana (Su A-51722) valued at RMB 172,000, and Changhe (Su A-T5045) valued at RMB 48,500. If unable to return them, compensate at the original price; 6. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company bear the various economic losses compensated to customers due to delayed delivery and project quality issues during the period Zhu Changchun operated Huaning Company, totaling RMB 1,060,082; 7. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company return the funds of Huaning Company that were misappropriated during the negotiation period from November 12, 2002, to January 23, 2003, totaling RMB 7,385,582.57; 8. Zhu Changchun and Zhu Ming'an pay Qian Bifang the consideration for the transfer of equity in Huayu Company, approximately RMB 6 million; 9. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company bear other concealed debts of Huaning Company incurred before January 23, 2003, and return concealed rights and interests of Huaning Company formed before January 23, 2003, approximately 70% of RMB 3.5 million, i.e., RMB 2.45 million; 10. Zhu Changchun return Qian Bifang's personal office and living supplies left at Huayu Company, valued at approximately RMB 50,000; 11. The total amount of claims in items 1 through 10 above is RMB 19,558,698.42. If the amount determined after audit exceeds this amount, the right to claim the excess is reserved; 12. The opposing party bear the litigation costs of this case.

The court of first instance held: The "Huaning Resolution" signed by Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang on November 12, 2002, and the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" signed under the auspices of the Jiangning District Court on January 23, 2003, represented the true intentions of both parties, did not violate relevant state laws and regulations, and were ratified by Wang Xianchen and Zhu Ming'an. They should be legally recognized as valid and effective. After the above resolutions were reached, both parties should enjoy rights and perform obligations in accordance with the agreed content. After the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" was reached, Qian Bifang, taking advantage of the favorable condition granted by the Jiangning District Court to handle the procedures for changing the equity and business registrations of the two companies, only processed the change of Zhu Changchun's equity in Huaning Company to the name of Wang Xianchen and changed the legal representative of Huaning Company to her father Qian Jiuzhong, while withholding documents including the agreement on the transfer of her equity in Huayu Company, failing to process the business registration change for the transfer of her equity in Huayu Company to the name of Zhu Ming'an. Furthermore, when the Jiangning District Court lifted the freeze on Huaning Company's bank deposits of RMB 13.65 million, she withdrew the RMB 5.2 million that should have been paid to Huayu Company, and directly asserted the claim against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau that had already been transferred to Huayu Company. These actions were all contrary to the principle of good faith. Qian Bifang's conduct of enjoying the rights granted by the resolutions without performing the agreed obligations was the root cause of the dispute. Qian Bifang should bear primary responsibility for this.

The focus of the dispute in this case is whether the claims in the main action by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company and the counterclaims by Qian Bifang and Huaning Company should be supported.

(I) Regarding whether the five claims in the main action by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company should be supported.

1. Regarding the claim for Qian Bifang and Huaning Company to jointly and severally pay RMB 5.2 million to Huayu Company. This RMB 5.2 million was an arrangement made by Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang to adjust the assets of Huaning Company and Huayu Company and to divide the RMB 13.65 million in bank deposits of Huaning Company that had been frozen by the Jiangning District Court. In the "Huaning Huayu Resolution," the two parties agreed that Huaning Company would give Huayu Company RMB 6 million. Later, during mediation by the Jiangning District Court, the parties agreed to adjust this to RMB 5.2 million, and Qian Bifang also issued a bank check accordingly. Now that Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company request a judgment ordering Huaning Company to pay Huayu Company RMB 5.2 million, this should be supported. Although the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" only provided for payment by Huaning Company to Huayu Company, in essence, it was the result of the transaction between Qian Bifang and Zhu Changchun regarding the equity of Huaning Company and Huayu Company. Therefore, Qian Bifang should bear joint and several liability for Huaning Company's payment of RMB 5.2 million to Huayu Company.

2. Regarding the claim for Huaning Company to transfer the ownership of villas located in the Bishuiwan Community, Jiangning District, Nanjing, specifically Numbers 96, 21, 49, 69, 70, 72, 16-2, 32-1, and 66-2, to Huayu Company, and if this cannot be done, for Qian Bifang and Huaning Company to jointly and severally pay consideration of approximately RMB 15 million (actual value to be calculated based on market appraised value). This claim is clearly stipulated in the "Huaning Huayu Resolution." Although during the mediation presided over by the Jiangning District Court, the court requested the two parties not to adjust the real estate of Huaning Company and Huayu Company, and Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang expressed their agreement not to adjust further, Zhu Changchun argues that his expression of intention not to adjust the two companies' real estate was a concession made based on the full performance of the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" and the need to quickly resolve the disputed issues. Now, Qian Bifang's dishonest behavior has seriously infringed upon the legitimate rights and interests of Zhu Changchun as the major shareholder of both companies. Therefore, he insists on performance according to the terms stipulated in the "Huaning Huayu Resolution." The court of first instance holds that the Jiangning District Court's request for Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang not to adjust the two companies' real estate does not have legally binding effect on either Zhu Changchun or Qian Bifang. In the interest of fairness and reasonableness, the request by Zhu Changchun to divide the assets of the two companies according to the agreed content of the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" should be supported.

3. Regarding the two claims for Huaning Company to transfer claims to Huayu Company, i.e., the claim against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau for RMB 16.5 million and 70% of the claim against the Jiangning District Land Bureau (i.e., RMB 14 million), to be transferred to Huayu Company. Because the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" clearly stipulates: "The claim of Huaning Company against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau in the amount of RMB 16.5 million (tentative) shall be pursued by Zhu Changchun. After paying the maintenance fund for the Bishuiwan Community (approximately RMB 3.5 million), the maintenance fund for the Ziwei Garden property (approximately RMB 1.96 million), the preliminary demolition costs for the Bishuiwan Community (RMB 1.2 million), and the road repair costs for the Bishuiwan Community (approximately RMB 1 million) within 30 days, the balance shall belong to Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company"; "If Huaning Company recovers the 460 mu plot of land at Chengbei Road, it shall pay Huayu Company RMB 14 million; if it recovers cash, it shall pay Huayu Company 70% of the amount." During the trial of the first instance, all parties expressed willingness to perform accordingly, so this should be supported.

4. Regarding the claim for Qian Bifang to assist Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company in transferring her 25% equity in Huayu Company (capital contribution of RMB 2.5 million) to the name of Zhu Ming'an. Qian Bifang has already transferred Zhu Changchun's equity in Huaning Company to the name of her mother without consideration and completed the business registration change. Therefore, according to the agreement in the "Huaning Huayu Resolution," she should transfer her equity in Huayu Company to Zhu Ming'an.

(II) Regarding whether the 11 counterclaims raised by Qian Bifang and Huaning Company should be supported.

1. Regarding the claim for Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company to bear 70% of the pre-paid 2003 corporate income tax of Huaning Company in the amount of RMB 242,304.49, i.e., RMB 169,613.14; and to bear 70% of the corporate income tax payable by Huaning Company that has not yet been determined due to incomplete documents, approximately RMB 120,000. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company proposed auditing the financial accounts of Huaning Company and Huayu Company to confirm the corporate income tax and other taxes payable by the two companies. However, according to the agreement between the parties that "70% of the 2003 corporate income tax of Huaning Company and Huayu Company shall be borne by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company; 30% shall be borne by Qian Bifang and Huaning Company," as long as Huaning Company and Huayu Company each present their tax payment certificates for 2003, the dispute can be resolved. Therefore, there is no need for an audit to determine this. Huaning Company provided evidence proving that it had paid a 2003 corporate income tax amount of RMB 206,789.70. According to the agreement between the parties, Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company should bear RMB 144,752.79. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company's request that Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company bear RMB 169,613.14 and RMB 12,000 in taxes lacks factual basis and is not supported. For the 2003 corporate income tax not yet paid by Huaning Company and Huayu Company, the parties may, after actual payment, demand the other party to handle it separately at the agreed ratio based on tax payment certificates.

2.  Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall bear 70% of the general business tax, stamp tax, etc. already paid by Huaning Company, totaling RMB 274,156.73, i.e., RMB 191,909.71; and bear 70% of other taxes payable by Huaning Company not yet confirmed by the tax authorities (business tax and surcharges, land value-added tax, stamp tax, etc.), approximately RMB 140,000. The Huaning Resolution had already taken tax factors into consideration, but did not stipulate how the parties should bear them. The Huaning-Huayu Resolution only specified the proportion of corporate income tax to be borne by each party, and Article 8 of that Resolution expressly stipulates: "Except for the items listed above, the other assets and liabilities of Huaning Company and Huayu Company shall be enjoyed and handled by each company itself." Therefore, this counterclaim of Qian Bifang and Huaning Company has no basis and is not supported.

3.  Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall bear the claim of approximately RMB 1.5 million for the portion exceeding RMB 5.5 million of various project payments due to Bishuiwan Residential Community and Ziwei Garden as of January 23, 2003, as confirmed by audit. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company requested an audit of Huaning Company's accounts to determine the amount of project payments due. According to the parties' agreement that "Huaning Company shall bear the unpaid project payments for the Bishuiwan and Ziwei Garden projects up to RMB 5.5 million, and the portion exceeding RMB 5.5 million shall be paid by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company, with payment of the project payments to be confirmed by Zhu Changchun and then paid by Qian Bifang," as long as Qian Bifang and Huaning Company produce the vouchers for project payments paid after confirmation by Zhu Changchun, the portion exceeding RMB 5.5 million shall be borne by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company, and no audit confirmation is needed. The total project payments paid by Huaning Company after January 23, 2003, as presented, amount to RMB 3,228,078, which has not yet reached RMB 5.5 million. Therefore, Qian Bifang and Huaning Company have no right to require Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company to bear this project payment.

4.  Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall return to Huaning Company all company documents and project materials. The account books and other materials of the two companies have been sealed with the court of first instance and will be returned to both parties after the judgment.

5.  Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall return to Huaning Company one Buick (license plate Su A-T6921) valued at RMB 357,368, one Iveco (license plate Su A-49440) valued at RMB 147,643, one Santana (license plate Su A-51722) valued at RMB 172,000, and one Changhe (license plate Su A-T5045) valued at RMB 48,500; if unable to return, compensate at the original price. Since all four vehicles were purchased before January 17, 2001, the Buick and Changhe have been awarded to employees by Huaning Company and are now privately owned, and the Huaning-Huayu Resolution expressly stipulates: "Except for the items listed above, the other assets and liabilities of Huaning Company and Huayu Company shall be enjoyed and handled by each company itself." Therefore, Qian Bifang and Huaning Company's claim for ownership of these four vehicles is not supported.

6.  Zhu Changchun shall bear the claim for various economic losses paid to customers due to delayed delivery and construction quality issues during his operation of Huaning Company, totaling RMB 1,060,082. Before January 23, 2003, Zhu Changchun was the chairman of Huaning Company, and Qian Bifang was the general manager of Huaning Company. On the financial expenditure vouchers of Huaning Company submitted by Qian Bifang, both Zhu Changchun's signature and Qian Bifang's signature appear, proving that it was the result of joint operation. After January 23, 2003, Huaning Company was fully managed by Qian Bifang, and the parties had expressly agreed: "Except for the items listed above, the other assets and liabilities of Huaning Company and Huayu Company shall be enjoyed and handled by each company itself." Now, Qian Bifang's request for Zhu Changchun to bear the alleged economic loss of RMB 1,060,082 has no factual or legal basis and is not supported.

7.  Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall return the funds of Huaning Company, amounting to RMB 7,385,582.57, allegedly misappropriated during the negotiation period from November 12, 2002, to January 23, 2003. Qian Bifang argues that after signing the Huaning-Huayu Resolution, upon reviewing Huaning Company's financial accounts, she discovered that during the period from November 12, 2002, to January 23, 2003, Zhu Changchun, taking advantage of his control over Huaning Company's operations and finances, used RMB 5,645,450.16 of Huaning Company's funds to pay project payments for Huayu Company, and that Huaning Company should also have RMB 1,740,132.41 in cash. She claims that she signed the Huaning-Huayu Resolution without knowledge of these facts, and that the RMB 5,645,450.16 and the RMB 1,740,132.41 in cash should not be subject to the agreement under the Huaning-Huayu Resolution, and therefore Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company should return the RMB 7,385,582.57. Zhu Changchun argues that the two parties jointly owned Huaning Company and Huayu Company, that the two companies were held by common shareholders, and that there were many connections in capital flows, personnel, etc. The financial vouchers and bank transfer check stubs of Huayu Company prove that from June 27, 2002, to December 31, 2002, Huayu Company made external payments on behalf of Huaning Company totaling RMB 30.718 million. Qian Bifang, as a minority shareholder of both companies, should have known the proportion of assets she was entitled to when dividing the assets of the two companies with the majority shareholder. Therefore, the Huaning-Huayu Resolution expressly stipulated: "As of January 22, 2003, the mutual claims and debts between Huaning Company and Huayu Company shall be set off against each other, and no further recourse shall be made." The court of first instance held that before January 23, 2003, both Huaning Company and Huayu Company were jointly operated and managed by Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang, and Qian Bifang should have known the situation of mutual payments between the two companies in their financial transactions. Moreover, the Huaning-Huayu Resolution expressly stipulated: "As of January 22, 2003, the mutual claims and debts between Huaning Company and Huayu Company shall be set off against each other, and no further recourse shall be made." Therefore, Qian Bifang's request to determine that the RMB 7,385,582.57 is not part of the Huaning-Huayu Resolution and that Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company should return the RMB 7,385,582.57 is not supported.

8.  Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall bear 70% of other concealed debts of Huaning Company incurred before January 23, 2003, and return the concealed rights and interests of Huaning Company formed before January 23, 2003, approximately 70% of RMB 3.5 million, i.e., RMB 2.45 million. Since Qian Bifang and Huaning Company failed to provide evidence to prove that Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company concealed Huaning Company's debts and rights and interests incurred before January 23, 2003, this claim has no factual basis and is not supported.

9.  Zhu Changchun and Zhu Ming'an shall pay Qian Bifang the consideration for the transfer of Huayu Company's equity, approximately RMB 6 million. The Huaning-Huayu Resolution stipulates: "Zhu Changchun shall transfer all his equity in Huaning Company (RMB 14 million) to third party Wang Xianchen at one time, and Qian Bifang shall transfer all her equity in Huayu Company (RMB 2.5 million) to Zhu Ming'an at one time, and separate equity transfer agreements shall be signed separately." Zhu Changchun transferred his equity in Huaning Company to Qian Bifang's mother, and Qian Bifang transferred her equity in Huayu Company to Zhu Changchun's father. The adjustment of the assets of the two companies by the parties was the consideration for the balanced transfer of equity. After Qian Bifang signed the Huaning-Huayu Resolution and related agreements at the Jiangning District Court, she transferred the equity of Huaning Company owned by Zhu Changchun to her mother's name without paying any consideration and completed the industrial and commercial registration change. Now she requests Zhu Changchun and Zhu Ming'an to pay her RMB 6 million as consideration for transferring 25% of Huayu Company's equity, which violates the parties' agreement. This request is not supported.

10. Qian Bifang's claim for the return of personal office and living items left by her at Huayu Company, valued at approximately RMB 50,000. Although this claim is not within the scope of the disputed case and should be dismissed, Zhu Changchun indicated during the trial that Qian Bifang's personal items could be retrieved at any time. Therefore, Qian Bifang should retrieve the items claimed on her own.

In summary, the claims of Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company are legitimate and well-founded and should be supported; the counterclaims of Qian Bifang and Huaning Company, insofar as they are legitimate and well-founded, are supported in accordance with law, and those without factual or legal basis are dismissed in accordance with law. Pursuant to Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 6, 8, Paragraph 1 of Article 44, Article 60, and Article 88 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:
1. Huaning Company shall pay Huayu Company RMB 5.2 million within 10 days after the judgment takes effect, and Qian Bifang shall bear joint and several liability for this payment obligation of Huaning Company.
2. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company shall, within 10 days after the judgment takes effect, transfer the ownership of Buildings 96, 21, 49, 69, 70, 72, 16-2, 32-1, and 66-2 of Bishuiwan Residential Community to Huayu Company; Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall, within 10 days after the judgment takes effect, transfer the ownership of the three storefronts, three villas, and six apartments in Bishuiwan West Garden to Huaning Company.
3. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company shall, within 10 days after the judgment takes effect, transfer the creditor's right of RMB 16.5 million against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau to Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company. Within 30 days of receiving this amount, Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall pay the maintenance fund for Bishuiwan Residential Community (RMB 3.5 million), the property maintenance fund for Ziwei Garden (RMB 1.96 million), the preliminary demolition costs for Bishuiwan Residential Community (RMB 1.2 million), and the road construction costs for Bishuiwan Residential Community (RMB 1 million).
4. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company shall, within 10 days after the judgment takes effect, transfer RMB 14 million of their creditor's right against the Jiangning District Land and Resources Bureau to Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company.
5. Qian Bifang shall, within 10 days after the judgment takes effect, transfer her 25% equity in Huayu Company (RMB 2.5 million) to Zhu Ming'an and complete the industrial and commercial registration change procedures.
6. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall, within 10 days after the judgment takes effect, pay Huaning Company the corporate income tax for the 2003 fiscal year already paid by Huaning Company, in the amount of RMB 144,752.79.
7. Huaning Company and Huayu Company shall, within 10 days after the judgment takes effect, retrieve their respective financial account books and other materials sealed with the court of first instance.
8. Qian Bifang shall retrieve her personal items stored at Huayu Company.
9. The other counterclaims of Qian Bifang and Huaning Company are dismissed.
The court acceptance fee for the main action is RMB 276,010, to be borne by Qian Bifang and Huaning Company; the court acceptance fee for the counterclaim is RMB 107,893.49, of which Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall bear RMB 26,974, and Qian Bifang and Huaning Company shall bear RMB 80,919.49.

Qian Bifang and Huaning Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing that the court of first instance refused to adopt their request for an audit of the two companies, resulting in a division of the companies' equity and assets without an audit, rendering the judgment erroneous. They requested that the court of second instance conduct an audit of the two companies, set aside the judgment of first instance, and render a new judgment in accordance with law. Their main grounds:

(I) All holdings of the judgment of first instance are erroneous.
1. The judgment ordering Qian Bifang and Huaning Company to jointly and severally pay Huayu Company RMB 5.2 million is improper. The reason Qian Bifang and Huaning Company did not pay this amount was that, according to the parties' agreement, Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company were obligated to deliver Huaning Company's certificates, seals, etc.; since they failed to perform this obligation, Qian Bifang and Huaning Company had the right of simultaneous performance defense against the payment of RMB 5.2 million. Furthermore, on the day after signing the Huaning-Huayu Resolution, Qian Bifang discovered that over RMB 5.6 million in Huaning Company's accounts had been arbitrarily used by Zhu Changchun to pay external project debts of Huayu Company. Therefore, even if Huaning Company paid the RMB 5.2 million, it should be offset.
2. The judgment of first instance is improper regarding the tax to be paid by Huaning Company. After signing the agreement, Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company failed to perform their obligations as agreed, and Huaning Company, while under Zhu Changchun's control, left behind serious tax issues. During the negotiation process, they failed to truthfully disclose the tax payable by Huaning Company, refused to deliver relevant project and financial materials, making it impossible for Huaning Company to accurately calculate the taxes due. As a result, Huaning Company could only prepay the 2003 tax of RMB 242,304.49 based on existing materials, and also paid RMB 12,000 in tax recovery and supplementary payments on behalf of Huayu Company. The agreement between the parties regarding taxes in the Huaning Resolution did not refer solely to "2003 corporate income tax" but included all taxes related to the three projects of Huaning and Huayu Companies. The judgment of first instance only partially supported Qian Bifang and Huaning Company's counterclaim regarding taxes, which is clearly unfair and inconsistent with the facts and the law. They request that the court of second instance order the opposing party to fully perform their tax obligations in accordance with the agreement. The opposing party shall bear 70% of the income tax prepaid by Huaning Company for 2003, amounting to RMB 242,304.49, and also require clarification that the unconfirmed tax payable by Huaning Company, once calculated or determined by the tax authorities, shall also be borne by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company at 70%.
3. Regarding Holding 2 of the judgment of first instance, that Qian Bifang and Huaning Company shall transfer ownership of Buildings 96, 21, 49, 69, 70, 72, 16-2, 32-1, and 66-2 of Bishuiwan Residential Community to Huayu Company, and Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall transfer ownership of the three storefronts, three villas, and six apartments in Bishuiwan West Garden to Huaning Company, this is inconsistent with the facts. During the mediation at the Jiangning District Court on January 23, 2003, both parties had already expressed their true intention that the above properties would no longer be adjusted, and this was recorded in the file at that time. Qian Bifang had submitted relevant evidence during the trial of first instance. Therefore, this holding of the court of first instance has no factual or legal basis and should be amended.
4. The judgment of first instance transferring the creditor's right of RMB 16.5 million held by Huaning Company against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau to Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company has no factual or legal basis. Zhu Changchun failed to fulfill his obligation to recover the creditor's right within the agreed period under the Huaning-Huayu Resolution, which is why Huaning Company notified Zhu Changchun in writing that the creditor's right would be recovered by Huaning Company itself. Moreover, to date, the Jiangning District Construction Bureau has not confirmed the actual amount of this creditor's right and has refused to pay Huaning Company. Because this creditor's right involves the rights of third parties and is in an uncertain state, it is inappropriate to handle it in this case. The judgment of first instance lacks factual and legal basis and should be dismissed or amended.
5. The court of first instance's judgment transferring RMB 14 million of the creditor's right held by Huaning Company against the Jiangning District Land and Resources Bureau to Huayu Company is problematic. This creditor's right involves the right to use 460 mu of land on Chengbei Road, which has not yet been resolved. According to the Huaning-Huayu Resolution, only if Huaning Company realizes this creditor's right can it pay 70% to Huayu Company. To date, Huaning Company has been actively asserting this right but has not yet realized it, so this holding of the court of first instance is currently premature. Moreover, the parties later had a special agreement on this issue, so if the judgment transfers the above creditor's right to Huayu Company, it should also simultaneously order it to pay Qian Bifang principal of RMB 6.24 million in accordance with the agreement.
6. Regarding Holding 5 of the judgment of first instance, ordering Qian Bifang to transfer her 25% equity in Huayu Company (RMB 2.5 million) to Zhu Ming'an, the Huaning-Huayu Resolution stipulates "Qian Bifang shall transfer her equity in Huayu Company to Zhu Ming'an," which expresses the intention of a transfer for consideration. Therefore, requesting this without Zhu Ming'an paying consideration has no factual or legal basis. If the other party considers it a gratuitous transfer, it would be a gift, but in this case, the subject matter of the gift, i.e., the 25% equity, has not been transferred, and the gift has not taken effect. Therefore, this claim of the opposing party should be dismissed. In fact, Qian Bifang transferring her equity in Huayu Company to Zhu Ming'an means she will no longer participate in any affairs of Huayu Company, and the other party should pay corresponding consideration of approximately RMB 6 million. The court of first instance's failure to support Qian Bifang's counterclaim that Zhu Changchun and Zhu Ming'an should pay corresponding consideration for acquiring Huayu Company's equity is improper and should be amended.

(2) The first-instance judgment did not support numerous counterclaims of Qian Bifang and Huaning Company, and should be amended. Specifically: 1. Regarding the project payment portion exceeding RMB 5.5 million. The "Supplementary Resolution" stipulated: "The unpaid project payments (various items) for Huaning Company's Ziwei Garden and Bishuiwan projects, as of January 22, 2003, for the portion below RMB 5.5 million, shall be paid by Huaning Company and Party B Qian Bifang; the portion exceeding RMB 5.5 million shall be borne by Party A Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company, and the payment of project funds shall be made by Party B after confirmation by Party A." Since Zhu Changchun refused to deliver project materials and relevant contracts and documents, the specific amount of outstanding project payments cannot be determined to date. A request is now made for the court of second instance to determine, through audit, the amount to be borne by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company. 2. Regarding the land use right of 28 mu of Bishuiwan. After the "Huaning Huayu Resolution," the parties made further agreements on this matter. Based on the agreement that "the issue of Huaning Company's land use right for 28 mu of Bishuiwan shall be handled by Party A; if it cannot be resolved, resulting in additional land transfer fees, fines, etc., shall be borne by Party A and Huayu Company," a request is made for the court of second instance to support Huaning Company's claim. 3. Regarding the return of Huaning Company's vehicles. All four vehicles owned by Huaning Company — Buick (Su A-T6921), Iveco (Su A-49440), Santana (Su A-51722), and Changhe (Su A-T5045) — are still occupied and used by the other party, which has refused to return them despite repeated demands. The first-instance judgment's finding that the company had rewarded the vehicles to employees is erroneous, because it is illegal for one person to arbitrarily decide to reward and distribute company fixed assets. The "Huaning Resolution" clearly stipulates that "private promises made by either party to subordinate staff under their respective management shall be fulfilled by the promisor personally, and shall not be paid from company property." Therefore, the other party has no right to dispose of them and should return them according to law. 4. The loss of RMB 1,060,082 caused to Huaning Company due to Zhu Changchun's poor management should be compensated according to law. During Zhu Changchun's management of Huaning Company, due to strategic errors in management, the repair costs and compensation payments resulting from refunds for garden area reductions and工程质量 issues totaled RMB 1,060,082, which should be borne by Zhu Changchun. 5. Regarding Zhu Changchun's unauthorized use of Huaning Company's funds, which should be returned and the resulting economic losses compensated. Zhu Changchun unauthorizedly used Huaning Company funds amounting to RMB 7,385,582.57. The "Huaning Resolution" of November 12, 2002 stipulated: "Before the company's audit report is issued, all external expenditures of the company shall be suspended immediately; Zhu Changchun shall not sign contracts or sell houses externally, and shall not transfer bank funds or real estate." After the resolution was signed, from November 12, 2002 to January 23, 2003, Zhu Changchun unauthorizedly used RMB 7,385,582.57 of Huaning Company's funds to pay outstanding engineering payments for Bishuiwan West Garden. However, on January 23, 2003, the parties signed the "Huaning Huayu Resolution," which stipulated: "The unsold portion of Bishuiwan West Garden community shall belong to Huayu Company, and Zhu Changchun shall no longer be a shareholder of Huaning Company." It can be seen that Zhu Changchun committed obvious infringement during the two-month period. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company should return the above funds and bear the economic losses caused to Huaning Company. 6. Regarding the issue of Zhu Changchun's claims and debts during his management of Huaning Company, a fair ruling should be made based on facts and law. Regarding the handling of concealed claims and debts during Zhu Changchun's control of Huaning Company: before January 23, 2003, Huaning Company was actually controlled and operated by Zhu Changchun. During the negotiations between the parties, Zhu Changchun concealed a large number of claims and debts. Apart from those listed above, the debts of Huaning Company concealed by Zhu Changchun should be borne by him personally, and the claims and income concealed by Zhu Changchun should be returned to Huaning Company.

In summary, the requests are: 1. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall bear 70% of Huaning Company's prepaid corporate income tax for 2003 of RMB 242,304.49, i.e., RMB 169,613.14; and bear 70% of the estimated corporate income tax that Huaning Company has not yet determined due to incomplete materials, approximately RMB 12,000. 2. Order Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company to bear: 70% of the total business tax, stamp tax, etc. already paid by Huaning Company of RMB 274,156.73, i.e., RMB 191,909.71; and 70% of other taxes payable by Huaning Company not yet confirmed by the tax authorities (business tax and surcharges, land value-added tax, stamp tax, etc.), approximately RMB 14,000. 3. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall bear the portion of various engineering payments confirmed by audit as payable by Huaning Company as of January 23, 2003, exceeding RMB 5.5 million, approximately RMB 1.5 million. 4. Return company materials and project materials belonging to Huaning Company; 5. Determine the land use right of 28 mu of Bishuiwan owned by Huaning Company according to law; the remaining issues of this land use right and all costs arising therefrom shall be borne by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company. 6. Return the vehicles owned by Huaning Company: Buick (Su A-T6921) valued at RMB 357,368; Iveco (Su A-49440) valued at RMB 147,643; Santana (Su A-51722) valued at RMB 172,000; Changhe (Su A-T5045) valued at RMB 48,500, or compensate at the original price if return is not possible. 7. Zhu Changchun shall bear the various economic losses compensated to customers during his management of Huaning Company due to delayed delivery and工程质量 issues, totaling RMB 1,060,082. 8. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall return the RMB 7,385,582.57 of Huaning Company funds encroached upon during the negotiations from November 12, 2002 to January 23, 2003 for engineering payments. 9. Zhu Changchun and Zhu Ming'an shall pay Qian Bifang the consideration for the transfer of her equity in Huayu Company of RMB 6 million. 10. Zhu Changchun shall bear the debts of Huaning Company concealed by him that arose before January 23, 2003, and return the concealed rights and interests of Huaning Company formed before January 23, 2003, approximately 70% of RMB 3.5 million, i.e., RMB 2.45 million. 11. Zhu Changchun shall return the approximately RMB 27,020,427.4 unauthorizedly withdrawn by him and bear the taxes on that amount. 12. Request the court of second instance to audit the property involved in this case according to law. 13. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company reserve the right to sue for any excess after the audit. 14. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company shall bear all litigation costs.

Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company argued in defense: The grounds of appeal by Qian Bifang and Huaning Company are untenable; the facts found in the first-instance judgment are clear and the law applied correctly, and should be affirmed. Specific reasons are as follows:

(1) The grounds of appeal by Qian Bifang and Huaning Company regarding taxes are untenable. The "Huaning Resolution" did not clearly stipulate the types of taxes and the proportion to be borne, nor was it actually performed, leading to subsequent disputes. The "Huaning Huayu Resolution" clearly stipulated that 70% of the 2003 annual income tax of Huaning and Huayu Companies would be borne by Huayu Company and 30% by Huaning Company. According to this agreement, taxes other than income tax cannot be borne in this proportion. The first-instance judgment's refusal to support Qian Bifang and Huaning Company's claims for taxes that have not actually occurred and for business tax, stamp tax, etc., other than income tax, fully complies with the parties' agreement on the scope of tax bearing. The appellant's grounds of appeal on this point are untenable and should be dismissed.

(2) Regarding the burden of the portion of project payments exceeding RMB 5.5 million. The "Supplementary Resolution" stipulated that as of January 23, 2003, the portion of project payments for Bishuiwan and Ziwei Garden developed by Huaning Company below RMB 5.5 million would be paid by Qian Bifang, and the portion exceeding that would be paid by Zhu Changchun, but Qian Bifang could only make payment after Zhu Changchun confirmed the amount. Qian Bifang failed to prove that the project payments she had made exceeded RMB 5.5 million. The first-instance judgment's dismissal of her claim on this point complies with the parties' agreement and the objective facts. This appeal request is meaningless and should be dismissed by the court of second instance.

(3) Regarding the return of Huaning Company's company materials and project materials, four vehicles, and Qian Bifang's personal belongings. Qian Bifang did not prove that all of Huaning Company's company materials and project materials were under Zhu Changchun's control. The first-instance court properly sealed the materials that had been confirmed and collected in the court and ordered the parties to retrieve them themselves. As for Qian Bifang's personal belongings stored at Huayu Company, the first-instance judgment ordered her to retrieve them herself, and Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company had no objection, so this appeal is meaningless. The four vehicles were all purchased before January 17, 2001, and had already been disposed of before the signing of the "Huaning Huayu Resolution." According to the parties' agreement, these are matters that need not be separately resolved, so the first-instance judgment was correct.

(4) Regarding the so-called loss of RMB 1,060,082 caused by Zhu Changchun to Huaning Company due to工程质量 compensation, the unauthorized use of Huaning Company funds of RMB 7,385,582.57, and the bearing of concealed debts of Huaning Company and return of concealed rights and interests of Huaning Company amounting to RMB 2.45 million. Before January 23, 2003, Qian Bifang directly participated in the daily operations of the company, so she should bear equal responsibility for the operational results of Huaning Company. Huaning Company and Huayu Company were companies controlled by Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang as joint shareholders, and there were many related financial transactions between the two companies. Precisely considering this special situation, the parties clearly stipulated in the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" that "the claims and debts between Huaning and Huayu Companies as of January 22, 2003 shall be offset against each other, and neither party shall pursue recovery from the other," and "except for items agreed upon in the resolution, the other assets and liabilities of the two companies shall be borne and handled by each company itself." Qian Bifang claims that Zhu Changchun should bear the concealed debts of Huaning Company and return the concealed claims of Huaning Company amounting to RMB 2.45 million, but to date, she has failed to provide evidence. Therefore, the first-instance judgment's findings on the above issues are not improper.

(5) Regarding the issue of Zhu Changchun and Zhu Ming'an paying Qian Bifang RMB 6 million as consideration for her 25% equity in Huayu Company. The "Huaning Huayu Resolution" and other relevant documents all indicate that Zhu Changchun transferred his 70% equity in Huaning Company to Qian Bifang's mother, Wang Xianchen, and Qian Bifang transferred her 25% equity in Huayu Company to Zhu Changchun's father, Zhu Ming'an, without either party needing to pay specific consideration. Zhu Changchun has already transferred his 70% equity in Huaning Company to Wang Xianchen free of charge as agreed, but Qian Bifang has not yet fulfilled her obligation. Therefore, she should promptly transfer her 25% equity in Huayu Company and has no right to demand consideration. The first-instance judgment on this item is correct and should be affirmed.

(6) Regarding the issue of the land use right of 28 mu of Bishuiwan and the request for Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company to return the unauthorized withdrawal of RMB 27,020,427.4. These issues were not claimed by Qian Bifang and Huaning Company in the first instance; they are new claims added in the second instance. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company do not respond to the added claims. According to the basic requirements of civil procedure, appeal requests cannot exceed the scope of first-instance claims. Therefore, the court of second instance should dismiss these appeal requests.

(7) Regarding the audit and the reservation of the right to sue by Qian Bifang and Huaning Company for the excess. The shareholders of both Huaning and Huayu Companies were Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang. When the parties adjusted their equity, they did not agree to adopt a method of dividing property based on audit conclusions, but rather based on the shareholders' understanding and approximate estimation of the companies, and on that basis, they formally signed the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" and other valid resolutions. Now that Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company have fully performed their obligations, the other party proposes to re-divide company property through audit, which is clearly unfair. Moreover, making a request for an audit as an independent claim in the second instance is also inappropriate. As for the so-called "reservation of the right to sue for the excess," this fully demonstrates that the other party still cannot clarify what their claims actually are; all the claims they raise on appeal are purely imaginary. Such claims can only be dismissed. The first-instance court's reasons for not supporting Qian Bifang and Huaning Company's request for an audit were appropriate and the conclusion correct, and we request the court of second instance to adopt this.

Other matters: all agree with the first-instance judgment.
