After the parties reached the agreement, Qian Bifang issued a "bad check for RMB 5.2 million," handled the procedures for changing Huaning Company's business registration, and transferred Zhu Changchun's 70% equity in Huaning Company to Wang Xianchen's name. Having already enjoyed all the rights under the agreement, she still filed an appeal, which shows a lack of basic good faith. In summary, the appeal requests of Qian Bifang and Huaning Company lack factual and legal basis and should all be dismissed.

The court found through trial: To implement the contents of the "Huaning Huayu Resolution," on January 23, 2003, Qian Bifang and Huaning Company, together with Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company, signed the "Agreement on the Handling of the Land Use Right Issue of 28 mu of Bishuiwan" and the "Agreement on the Handling of the 460 mu Plot on Chengbei Road." Regarding the 460 mu plot on Chengbei Road, i.e., Huaning Company's claim against the Jiangning District Land Bureau, the parties agreed: The land is in Huaning Company's name. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company agreed that Huaning Company would recover it. If the land is recovered and developed by Huaning Company, Huaning Company shall pay Huayu Company RMB 14 million; if cash is recovered, 70% shall be given to Huayu Company; if, due to Zhu Changchun's fault, Huaning Company neither recovers the land nor obtains cash, Zhu Changchun shall compensate Qian Bifang RMB 6.24 million.

Regarding Huaning Company's claim against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau, on January 23, 2003, Qian Bifang and Huaning Company, together with Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company, signed the "Huaning Huayu Resolution," which stipulated that this claim would be recovered by Zhu Changchun. On the same day, the "Claim Assignment and Collection Authorization Agreement" signed by the parties and the "Notice of Claim Assignment" issued to the Jiangning District Construction Bureau expressed the intention to assign the claim, partially assign it, and authorize collection.

After Qian Bifang filed a civil lawsuit with the Jiangning District Court, the Jiangning District Court, at Qian Bifang's request, froze Huaning Company's bank deposits totaling RMB 13,754,252.

Item 5 of Qian Bifang's appeal request regarding the land use right of 28 mu of Bishuiwan and Item 11 regarding the request for Zhu Changchun to return the approximately RMB 27,020,427.4 unauthorizedly withdrawn and bear the taxes on that amount are new claims added in the second instance. Moreover, regarding the withdrawal of approximately RMB 27,020,427.4 by Zhu Changchun, Qian Bifang was already clearly aware of this before the signing of the "Huaning Huayu Resolution."

The other facts found by this court are the same as those found by the first-instance court.

This court holds: As the sole shareholders of Huaning Company and Huayu Company, Zhu Changchun and Qian Bifang convened shareholders' meetings and formed resolutions, reaching the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" and related agreements on the adjustment of equity and assets of the two companies. These acts comply with legal provisions and should be deemed valid.

The focus of the dispute between the parties is whether an audit should be conducted to resolve this case, how to bear relevant amounts such as taxes and project payments, how to dispose of chattels such as related real estate and vehicles, whether Zhu Changchun and Zhu Ming'an should pay consideration for Qian Bifang's transfer of her 25% equity in Huayu Company, and whether related claims should be assigned:

(1) Whether an audit should be conducted to resolve this case.

At the first instance, Qian Bifang requested an audit of the assets of the two companies on the grounds that the amount of taxes payable could not be accurately calculated by themselves. The first-instance court held that the existing agreements were sufficient to determine how to resolve tax disputes between the parties, so it did not support the audit request. This handling was not improper. Qian Bifang reiterated the audit request at the second instance, but provided no new or more compelling reasons. Zhu Changchun's side argued that Zhu and Qian, as shareholders of both companies, had been involved in operations and were familiar with the companies' basic circumstances; all agreements signed on the division of equity were based on negotiation without audit; and Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company had fully performed their obligations, so they opposed the audit. Zhu Changchun's argument is well-founded and should be adopted.

(2) How to bear relevant amounts such as taxes and project payments.

1. Regarding the taxes payable by Huaning Company. The "Huaning Huayu Resolution" only stipulated the proportion of the 2003 annual corporate income tax to be borne by the two companies, and did not specifically and clearly stipulate other taxes besides corporate income tax. The first-instance judgment, based on the parties' agreement that "except for the items listed above, the other assets and liabilities of Huaning Company and Huayu Company shall be enjoyed and handled by each company itself," did not support Qian Bifang and Huaning Company's claims for taxes that had not actually occurred and for business tax, stamp tax, etc., other than corporate income tax. This was not improper. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company's grounds of appeal on this point are untenable and are dismissed.

2. Whether Qian Bifang and Huaning Company should jointly and severally pay Huayu Company RMB 5.2 million. According to the "Huaning Huayu Resolution," Huaning Company should pay Huayu Company RMB 6 million, which was later adjusted to RMB 5.2 million by mutual agreement. Huaning Company should pay this amount as agreed. As the obligee, Huayu Company's claim at the first instance was exactly RMB 5.2 million, and the first-instance judgment's support of this claim was not improper. Qian Bifang and Huaning Company's grounds of appeal on this point are untenable and are dismissed.

3. Regarding the burden of the portion of project payments exceeding RMB 5.5 million. The parties did agree that the portion of Bishuiwan project payments exceeding RMB 5.5 million would be borne by Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company. However, the first-instance court found that the project payments Qian Bifang had actually paid were only over RMB 3 million, which had not yet reached the condition for Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company to bear the burden. Therefore, her claim that the other party should bear approximately RMB 1.5 million is inconsistent with the facts, and the first-instance court was correct not to support it.

4. Regarding the bearing of the loss of RMB 1,060,082 for工程质量 compensation of Huaning Company, whether Zhu Changchun unauthorizedly used Huaning Company funds of RMB 7,385,582.57, and whether Zhu Changchun should bear the concealed debts of Huaning Company and return the concealed rights and interests of Huaning Company amounting to RMB 2.45 million. The problematic projects of Huaning Company were constructed during the joint operation of both parties. The act of Zhu Changchun withdrawing Huaning Company funds of RMB 7,385,582.57 also occurred before the signing of the "Huaning Huayu Resolution." The "Huaning Huayu Resolution" clearly stipulated that the claims and debts between the two companies as of January 22, 2003 were offset against each other, with no recovery, and each company would bear and handle its own other assets and liabilities except for the agreed items. Additionally, although Qian Bifang claimed that Zhu Changchun should bear the concealed debts of Huaning Company and return the concealed claims of Huaning Company amounting to RMB 2.45 million, she never provided evidence. Therefore, the first-instance judgment's dismissal of Qian Bifang's above counterclaims was not improper.

(3) Whether some real estate under the names of the two companies should be swapped and adjusted, and whether Huaning Company's company materials and project materials, four vehicles, and Qian Bifang's personal belongings should be returned.

Zhu Changchun argued that in the investigation transcript of the Jiangning District People's Court, although both parties had expressed an intention that the relevant properties would no longer be adjusted, because the other party completely failed to perform its obligations, he requested that performance still be carried out in accordance with the "Huaning Huayu Resolution." The first-instance court held that the statement that the relevant properties would no longer be adjusted was merely an expression made by both parties during the investigation by the Jiangning District People's Court, not a formal agreement, and thus did not have binding force on the parties. Taking into account the actual performance status of both parties, the first-instance court supported Zhu Changchun's request and ordered both parties to perform in accordance with the "Huaning Huayu Resolution," which was not improper. Qian Bifang appealed this ruling but failed to provide evidence at the second instance, so her request was not supported.

The first-instance court had already ruled that both parties should retrieve their materials sealed by the court on their own. Since Qian Bifang and Huaning Company had no evidence that Huayu Company still had materials belonging to Huaning Company, they should have complied with that ruling. Qian Bifang requested the return of her personal belongings stored at Huayu Company. The first-instance court had already ordered her to retrieve them on her own, and Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company did not raise any objection. There was no need to appeal this claim that had already been supported; she could simply retrieve the items.

Regarding the disposal of four motor vehicles registered under Huaning Company's name, this occurred before the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" was signed. Qian Bifang, as a shareholder who had been continuously involved in the company's operations, should have known about this. According to the agreement between the parties, this was an issue to be borne and handled by Huaning Company itself.

Therefore, the first-instance court's handling of the above issues was not improper.

(4) The issue of whether Zhu Changchun and Zhu Ming'an should pay RMB 6,000,000 as consideration for Qian Bifang's transfer of her 25% equity in Huayu Company.

Qian Bifang and Zhu Changchun were joint shareholders of Huaning Company and Huayu Company. The "Huaning Huayu Resolution" and other related documents all indicated that when the two companies were undergoing equity adjustment and asset division, the consideration for the equity transfer had already been taken into account, and neither party needed to pay separate consideration for it. The parties agreed that Zhu Changchun would transfer his 70% equity in Huaning Company to Qian Bifang's mother, Wang Xianchen, and Qian Bifang would transfer her 25% equity in Huayu Company to Zhu Changchun's father, Zhu Ming'an. Since Zhu Changchun had already transferred his 70% equity in Huaning Company to Wang Xianchen without consideration as agreed, but Qian Bifang had delayed in performing her obligations and further demanded RMB 6,000,000 as consideration from the other party, her request lacked factual and legal basis and was not supported.

(5) The issue of how to handle the claims against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau and the Jiangning District Bureau of Land and Resources.

There was no dispute between the parties regarding the allocation after the successful realization of these two claims. That is, both parties agreed that after the claim against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau was realized, after deducting four items (the maintenance fund for the Bishuiwan residential area, the maintenance fund for the Ziwei Garden residential area, the preliminary demolition costs for the Bishuiwan residential area, and the road construction costs for the Bishuiwan residential area), the balance would belong to Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company. After the claim against the Jiangning District Bureau of Land and Resources was realized, the parties had also reached an agreement on the allocation ratio of land or cash. However, before the claims were realized, the parties disagreed on whether an assignment of claims had occurred between Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company on the one hand, and Qian Bifang and Huaning Company on the other, specifically on whose behalf the claim should now be asserted and against whom.

Based on the facts found by the first-instance court and this Court, the claim against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau was originally under Huaning Company's name. In the multiple agreements and documents signed by the parties in this case, this claim was mentioned. Specifically, the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" stipulated that Zhu Changchun would be responsible for recovering this claim, which did not reflect an intention to assign the claim. The "Agreement on Assignment of Claims and Authorization for Collection" and the "Notice of Assignment of Claims" issued to the Jiangning District Construction Bureau contained different expressions regarding assignment of claims, authorization for collection, and partial assignment. Thus, there was unclear agreement and inconsistent expression of intent between the parties on whether the claim was assigned, and if so, whether it was a full or partial assignment. The first-instance court indicated that after the dispute arose, both parties agreed to perform in accordance with the "Huaning Huayu Resolution," and therefore the determination should be made based on the content of that resolution, and ruled that the claim belonged to Zhu Changchun. However, following the reasoning set forth by the first-instance court, if the matter were handled in accordance with the "Huaning Huayu Resolution," the claim should still belong to Huaning Company, with Zhu Changchun only responsible for recovering it, and the court should not have ruled that the claim was assigned. Huaning Company's ground for appeal on this issue was well-founded and was supported. The first-instance court's handling was erroneous and should be modified.

Regarding the claim against the Jiangning District Bureau of Land and Resources, i.e., the 460 mu plot on North Chengbei Road, according to the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" and the "Agreement on Handling the 460 mu Plot on North Chengbei Road," the land was registered under Huaning Company's name. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company agreed that Huaning Company would recover the land, and after recovery, Huaning Company would compensate Huayu Company. It follows that the claim should be asserted externally against the debtor in the name of Huaning Company, and there was no clear expression of assignment of the claim. The first-instance court affirmed the validity of the "Huaning Huayu Resolution" but also ruled to assign the claim to Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company, which was inconsistent with the agreed content of the parties. The ground for appeal by Qian Bifang and Huaning Company requesting modification of this ruling was well-founded and should be supported.

(6) The issues concerning the right to use the 28 mu plot of land at Bishuiwan and Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company's return of the RMB 27,020,427.4 they had withdrawn without authorization.

These two claims were newly added by Qian Bifang and Huaning Company at the second instance. Zhu Changchun and Huayu Company did not acknowledge them, so the parties should resolve these matters through negotiation or may pursue other legal remedies.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Affirm Items 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 of Civil Judgment (2004) SMCZEZD No. 6 of the Jiangsu High People's Court.

2. Modify Item 3 of Civil Judgment (2004) SMCZEZD No. 6 of the Jiangsu High People's Court to read: The claim of Jiangsu Huaning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. against the Jiangning District Construction Bureau of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province shall be performed in accordance with Article 2, Paragraph 6 of the "Resolution of the Shareholders' Meeting of Jiangsu Huaning Huayu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd."

3. Modify Item 4 of Civil Judgment (2004) SMCZEZD No. 6 of the Jiangsu High People's Court to read: The claim of Jiangsu Huaning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. against the Jiangning District Bureau of Land and Resources Administration of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province shall be performed in accordance with Article 2, Paragraph 2 of the "Resolution of the Shareholders' Meeting of Jiangsu Huaning Huayu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd."

4. Dismiss the other appeal requests of Qian Bifang and Jiangsu Huaning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

The court acceptance fee for the first-instance principal claim is RMB 276,010, of which RMB 110,404 shall be borne by Qian Bifang and Jiangsu Huaning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and RMB 165,606 shall be borne by Zhu Changchun and Jiangsu Huayu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. The court acceptance fee for the first-instance counterclaim is RMB 107,893.49, to be executed in accordance with the first-instance judgment. The court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 383,903.49, of which RMB 218,297.49 shall be borne by Qian Bifang and Jiangsu Huaning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and RMB 165,606 shall be borne by Zhu Changchun and Jiangsu Huayu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.
